notes_list.title: SN2 Reaction Mechanism
notes_list.basic_overview: SN2 is a concerted bimolecular substitution in which nucleophile attack and leaving-group departure occur in one elementary step.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Backside attack gives inversion of configuration at the reacting center. Steric hindrance strongly affects rate.
notes_list.examples: Methyl and primary alkyl halides react readily with strong nucleophiles; tertiary centers are generally unsuitable for SN2.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Polar aprotic solvents often increase anionic nucleophilicity by reducing strong hydrogen-bond solvation. Good leaving groups and unhindered substrates favor SN2.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Nucleophile approaches 180° to C–LG bond. 2. New C–Nu bond forms while C–LG breaks. 3. Product forms with inversion.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Ideal rate law: rate = k[RX][Nu−]. One transition state contains both nucleophile and leaving group bonding interactions.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Predict inversion, substrate order and solvent effects.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not call a reaction SN2 merely because a strong nucleophile is present; substrate geometry and sterics matter.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
